Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the UAE's reply with the bat. The Pakistani players spread out and take their respective fielding positions. Muhammad Waseem and Alishan Sharafu are the openers for the United Arab Emirates. Shaheen Afridi to begin with the new ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right. Pakistan have managed to post a challenging total and the UAE will have to bat out of their comfort zone to hunt this target down. Over-reliance on Muhammad Waseem and Asif Khan have put on a lot of strain on the rest of the batting unit and it is now time for them to step up. FYI, chasing has been extremely difficult in Sharjah and anything more than 150 has not been hunted down in this particular tri-series. It will be a real test of nerves on how the UAE batters handle the pressure against a spirited Pakistani bowling unit. An exciting run chase coming up on the other side. Stay tuned.

Haider Ali of UAE is up for a quick chat. He points out that the pitch had a bit of moisture in it, so they wanted to go hard on the batters as it is a must-win match for them. Admits that they were sloppy in the field which turned out to be very costly for them towards the backend. Says they know how dangerous someone like Fakhar Zaman and Nawaz can be in the death overs. Admits that if those catches had been taken, they could have easily restricted Pakistan to somewhere around 140-150. Ends by saying that they have no choice now and will try hard to win this.

When pressure creeps in such a situation, it either pushes you further down, or a fearless knock from someone lifts the team up. 74/4 became 80/5, but then came the momentum-changing partnership between Fakhar Zaman and Mohammad Nawaz towards the backend. Pakistan could have lost a couple of more wickets pretty soon, but both Fakhar and Nawaz being provided a reprieve in two consecutive deliveries meant they took the bowlers to the cleaners in the last five overs. In fact, the last two overs went for 42 runs which totally swung the momentum Pakistan's way.

Two of their batters - Haris and Fakhar - in a bit of a lean patch lately, tried to form an alliance which was crucial from Pakistan's perspective. They looked all but convincing with the ball slightly holding when spin formed a tandem in middle overs. Runs didn't come at a fair clip, and what the UAE bowlers did well was they didn't allow easy singles, and the streak of dots further plugged the scoring rate a bit. In that 7-10 over phase, Pakistan could only muster up 24 runs, while also losing Haris after a scratchy knock.

Credits should be given where it is due. UAE looked disciplined early doors with the new ball. There was just enough evident movement off the deck, which kept the batters honest. Ayub and Farhan tried to take off, but yet again, the opening stand for Pakistan couldn't see through the Powerplay successfully. Junaid and Rohid relentlessly tested those outside edges, drawing out false strokes, and with Agha too, gone early, this pushed Pakistan massively on the back foot. The score after six overs read 50/3, but in all fairness, it was not at all the best of Powerplays for them with the bat.

A very strong finish for Pakistan in the end, but who would have thought that from a precarious position of being 80/5 in the 12th over, the tourists would end up posting in north of 170, without losing a single wicket? A bit of inexperienced bowling in the death overs by the UAE bowlers as they were a bit too predictable in their lines and lengths. And more importantly, they did not vary the pace as they did in the first 15 overs or so, which resulted in Fakhar and Nawaz feasting on anything loose thrown at them.

FOUR! What a knock from Fakhar! Very full now, outside off. Fakhar Zaman gets the width and the length in the arc, clears the front leg away and smashes it over cover for a cracking boundary. 22 off the final over! PAKISTAN FINISH ON 171/5.

UAE head coach, Lalchand Rajput is up for a quick chat with the broadcasters. He reflects that the boys have played really well and have given tough times to the opposition. Admits that they haven't quite managed to cross the line yet, but hopes that day will come soon. Adds it is a huge platform for the boys and they need to enjoy playing cricket. Also details that they do not get plenty of chances to play against Test-playing nations and says they just need to play their best cricket when they enter the field. Adds they have been preparing hard for the upcoming Asia Cup and hopes that the team will find some momentum in the remaining couple of fixtures

TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin goes in favor of Pakistan and Salman Agha elects to BAT first.

Bored? That’s how every day feels when the weekend refuses to show up. Anyway, while we wait for the toss update from this clash, let’s shift our focus for a bit to the UK, where hosts England are chasing white-ball redemption in a 3-ODI series against South Africa. The Proteas claimed the opening game in style, and right now, the second ODI is in full swing at the Home of Cricket, Lord's. England won the toss and elected to bowl. Already, the first inning is more than halfway through. You can catch every bit of that action by simply switching tabs.

Batting against the new ball has been tricky on the slowish Sharjah surface, as history would suggest too. Once the hardness and shine wear off though, scoring becomes a little more comfortable. Interestingly, the chasing side has come up short in all four games so far, with the average second innings total hovering just north of 150, hinting that batting first has offered the upper hand. Pakistan arrive with their agenda to play better all-round cricket. UAE will take heart from their last clash with Pakistan when they pushed the Men In Green and looked on course in a chase of over 200, but somehow fell short. Will that script change? Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

Momentum has been hard to sustain for the UAE. Too much weight has fallen on Muhammad Waseem and Asif Khan, though Rahul Chopra's effort last time out offered a timely boost. They’ve started brightly - 54 and 66 in the Powerplay - showing plenty of spark against the challenging new ball phase, largely thanks to Waseem’s aggression. But the middle overs have turned into a minefield with wickets falling in clusters. It’s still a young side, still stitching together the right balance in both departments, and will be eager to iron out these wrinkles this time around.

Pakistan remain on top of the table, yet none of their batters sit among the top three scorers or have reached triple figures. Saim Ayub has been the pick of the lot with skipper Salman Agha in support, but the rest of the batting has lacked bite. They’ve coughed up a couple of wickets inside the Powerplay on average, and still chase that elusive solid start. Senior pro Fakhar Zaman and the young dasher Mohammad Haris have both been off the boil, and that’s left a few dents in the batting blueprint. The saving grace has been their bowling, with both wins coming while defending, and Haris Rauf spearheading the charge. But they will need a collective batting effort if they’re to carry this momentum all the way.

Pakistan suffered a stinging setback at the hands of Afghanistan, yet they remain at the top of the table courtesy of a healthier net run rate. A win tonight punches their ticket straight to Sunday’s final. For the UAE, though, with two losses on the trot, this is virtually a do-or-die fixture. Win to keep the flame alive. Lose and bow out. For the home team, it is about testing their depth against stiffer challenges and finding out exactly where they stand. So far, the answers have been hard to come by, but they have indeed displayed some valor and fight. They will want to stride in with sharper plans and a much more polished display.

Action returns to the iconic Sharjah Cricket Stadium after a day’s break as the Tri-Series in the Emirates rolls on. With less than a week remaining for the upcoming Asia Cup in this nation, teams are preparing hard to refine combinations and gain the momentum for that marquee event. We are in the reverse fixtures, and in Match 5, it’s Pakistan taking on the hosts, the United Arab Emirates. On that note, hello and welcome to our coverage. We are glad to have you all with us.

Pakistan and the United Arab Emirates will clash in the fifth match of the T20I Tri-Series in Sharjah, with both teams looking to make an impact. Pakistan, currently at the top in the standings with four points from three games, will be eager to bounce back after their first defeat in the series, an 18-run setback against Afghanistan. A victory over the UAE would all but secure their place in the finals. Pakistan's batting lineup has been impressive, with opener Saim Ayub leading the charge with 83 runs from three innings. Captain Salman Agha has also been consistent, contributing 78 runs across three innings. Hasan Nawaz has provided solidity to the batting lineup, gathering 74 runs from three appearances. The middle order, featuring Mohammad Haris and Mohammad Nawaz, offers attacking intent when needed. Pakistan's bowling unit has been a strength, with Haris Rauf claiming four scalps from two outings. Faheem Ashraf and Mohammad Nawaz have excelled on the slower surfaces, taking eight wickets between them. However, pace leader Shaheen Afridi will be keen to make a bigger impact in the upcoming fixtures. The UAE, on the other hand, have struggled badly in the tri-series, losing both their opening matches. They still have a mathematical chance of reaching the finals, but it will require big wins in their remaining games. Skipper Muhammad Waseem has carried the batting load, scoring 100 runs from two innings, while Asif Khan has made a significant impact with his rapid scoring. Rahul Chopra has also been a reliable option, and the UAE will count on him to produce something special. The pitch is expected to help spinners, which could play to the advantage of both teams. Pakistan will look to exploit this with their experienced spin department, while UAE's Saghir Khan, who has claimed five wickets so far, could be a key player. With Pakistan looking to bounce back and the UAE fighting to stay alive, the match promises to be an exciting encounter.
